citation.authors: Swaile DF, Elstun LT, Benzing KW

record.population: Male panellists in hot-room sweat tests; ethnicity not stated in the abstract
record.design: Gravimetric (sweat weight) tests of an over-the-counter antiperspirant against placebo and against a prescription aluminium chloride product
record.finding: The over-the-counter "clinical strength" antiperspirant reduced sweat rate on average 34% more than the prescription product and caused significantly less skin irritation; the authors say it can be an alternative for heavy sweating.
record.note: Men only; affiliations and funding not checked; placebo group also showed large sweat falls.
